criteria.criterion: Use official npm Registry response at specified URL
criteria.description: Agent attempts to consult the official npm Registry JSON response from https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript/latest and uses it as the source for all requested fields. Full credit if the agent clearly indicates the URL is inaccessible (e.g., downtime/network/CAPTCHA/blocking) and therefore the registry response could not be retrieved. Partial credit if another source is used only after a clear attempt to use the specified URL (and the limitation is explained). No credit if values are provided without evidence or without attempting the specified URL.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots 1 and 2 both show a raw JSON document with npm-registry-typical fields (e.g., _id, name, version, license, dist.tarball pointing to https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript/-/typescript-7.0.2.tgz). Action History shows the agent was on https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript/latest and scrolled. Latest evidence: Screenshot 2 continues to show the same registry-style JSON.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The action history directly indicates use of the official npm registry /latest endpoint, and the screenshots are consistent with an npm Registry response (including registry tarball URL). No evidence of using alternative sources. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a page rendering raw JSON (with a visible “Pretty-print” checkbox at top). In the JSON, fields like "bin":{"tsc":"bin/tsc"...}, "bugs":{"url":"https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues"}, and a "dist" object are visible. The content appears consistent with an npm registry JSON response for TypeScript, but the browser address bar / URL is not visible in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot supports that the agent is viewing an npm-style JSON payload that includes typical registry fields (e.g., dist, maintainers, license). However, because the URL bar is not visible, the screenshot alone cannot confirm it is specifically from https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript/latest. Still, it is consistent with the official registry response format.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent/predicted output cites the specific URL. The screenshot does not display the URL, so that specific claim is not directly verifiable from pixels (though the JSON format aligns with it).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a raw JSON response consistent with an npm registry endpoint (plain text JSON). Visible fields include keys like "_id":"typescript@7.0.2", "name":"typescript", "version":"7.0.2", "license":"Apache-2.0", and a "dist" object containing "tarball":"https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript/-/typescript-7.0.2.tgz", "fileCount":416, and "unpackedSize":13134585. The browser UI shows a "Pretty-print" checkbox at the top, typical of viewing JSON directly in a browser.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The visible content is clearly the official npm Registry-style JSON for TypeScript (it includes registry.npmjs.org tarball URL and standard npm metadata). While the screenshot itself does not show the exact address bar URL, the content matches what would come from https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript/latest, supporting that the agent used the correct source.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims the source URL explicitly; the screenshot does not show the URL bar, but the JSON content (registry tarball URL, standard fields) is consistent with npm registry output, so no direct contradiction is visible.
